## Grammar

Basic word order is SVO; it has prepositions. In the noun phrase: possessor before the possessed; noun before the adjective; noun before the demonstrative; numeral before the noun; noun before the relative clause. Overall it is head-initial.
It has no definite article, an indefinite article, no case marking on nouns, no alignment marking (subject and object are not told apart by form), singular and plural, no gender or noun classes.
Verbs mark past and perfective; there are no evidentials. Negation uses a negator before the verb; yes/no questions use intonation alone. Verbs agree with the subject by suffixes; not with the object.
Other features: pronouns can be dropped; numeral classifiers; serial verbs; adjectives that behave like verbs; a periphrastic causative; no passive; question words left in place; a decimal counting base; a 'have' verb for possession.
Measured morphology: 10 live grammatical markers, mean bondedness 0.1 (0 free word … 3 fused), 0 paradigm cells, 0 of them with allomorphy.
